What to do

  1. Stop the sitewide 20% discount. Discounts cost $232K of profit. The September test showed 20% off moved conversion by only +0.77 points (p = 0.335, not significant) while cutting product profit by $6.68 per customer (95% CI -9.65 to -3.71).
  2. Re-bid heavy-parcel shipping. Since April 2025 heavy orders go to SwiftShip at about twice the old rate. Shipping them at the ParcelPro heavy rate would have saved $85K in 2025.
  3. Claim the Aurora lamp defect from the supplier. Aurora Standing Lamp returns jumped from 2.5% to 23.6%; 246 units came back 'Defective - flickering' (May to Oct 2025 batch), costing $51K. Recover the cost and add an incoming quality check.
  4. Price Smart Home for margin, not just volume. Smart Home earns about 20% product margin and grew to about a quarter of sales; the mix shift cost $97K. Review pricing, bundles and ad spend for the category.
  5. Fix the dashboard before the next board meeting. The current dashboard reads the raw exports and shows 21.8% growth instead of 18.8%: orders exported by both systems during the migration add about $75K of revenue that never happened.

Act 2: the follow-up test

Jan to Apr 2026 · 89,405 visitors · three arms

  1. Ship the new product page (C), starting with mobile. Conversion rose from 3.43% to 3.79% (+10.6%, p = 0.0171, below the 0.025 bar for two comparisons). On mobile the lift was +21.9%. Profit per visitor: +$0.34 (97.5% CI -0.108 to 0.799): likely positive, about $107K a year, with no discount and no rise in returns.
  2. Do not launch the 10% off banner (B). Conversion +5.5% (p = 0.2128, not significant) and profit per visitor fell $0.97 (CI -1.35 to -0.584): about $301K a year lost. Its strong first weeks were a novelty effect.
  3. Keep the testing rules. Size the test before launch, check the split, remove bots and duplicate visitors, and decide only at the planned end date.

Act 3: which customers to invest in

5,285 customers who bought in 2024-2025

  1. Protect the Champions. The top 20% of customers earn 60.4% of profit. Champions are 848 customers worth about $222 each next year: early access and service, not discounts.
  2. Turn new customers into second-time buyers. New / promising customers are worth about $135 each next year, more than Loyal ones. A welcome series that earns the second order is the best use of budget (up to $40 per customer).
  3. Move budget from Paid Social to Email & Referral. A 2024 Paid Social customer earned $211 over two years, against $211 of 2025 spend per new customer. Email & Referral: $375 earned for $96.
  4. Target with the model, not past spend. Picking the top 20% by the model reached 49.3% of the next half-year's profit, vs 39.5% with RFM segments and 34.8% by past profit.
Built from the Harbor & Hearth warehouse by run_pipeline.py. All data is synthetic. Contribution profit = net sales - refunds - product cost (net of resellable returns) - shipping; marketing is reported separately.
